PullRequest.Title: sessions: fix: Open Agents Window shortcut does nothing while hidden
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #340127

On macOS, a system-wide keybinding for **Open Agents Window** did nothing while VS Code was hidden (Cmd+H) and the Agents window was already open. All windows of a hidden app count as invisible, and Electron ignores a request to focus an invisible window. VS Code's force focus does un-hide the app, but macOS then focuses whichever window was active before hiding, because un-hiding happens asynchronously.

### Changes

- **`BaseWindow.focus()`** in `windowImpl.ts`: with `FocusMode.Force` on macOS, if the app is hidden, show the target window before stealing focus, so that window is the one that ends up focused. This also fixes `workbench.action.focusWindow` (and other force-focus callers) while the app is hidden. Nothing changes when the app isn't hidden.
- **`NativeHostMainService.openAgentsWindow()`**: reveal the Agents window with `FocusMode.Force` instead of the default transfer focus. Every caller is an explicit request to open or show the Agents window, and when VS Code is already active the focus steal does nothing extra.
- **Docs**: a note in the "Gotchas for future work" section of the system-wide keybindings spec, saying that commands that show UI from a system-wide keybinding must use force focus. Also one sentence in `src/vs/sessions/SYSTEM_WIDE_KEYBINDING.md`.

`GlobalKeybindingsMainService.onTrigger` still intentionally doesn't focus the routing window, to avoid flicker.

### How to test

1. On macOS, add this to `keybindings.json`:
   ```jsonc
   { "key": "ctrl+cmd+a", "command": "workbench.action.openAgentsWindow", "systemWide": true }
   ```
2. Open the Agents window and an editor window, then click into the editor window.
3. Press Cmd+H to hide VS Code, then press Ctrl+Cmd+A.
4. VS Code should come back with the **Agents window** in front and focused. Before this change, nothing happened.
5. The shortcut should still focus the Agents window when VS Code is in the foreground, and when it is behind another app.

### Validation

`CodeWindow.focus` and `NativeHostMainService.openAgentsWindow` have no unit tests because they need real Electron, so this was validated manually:

- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. It reported 6 errors in unrelated agent-host files (`copilotSessionLauncher.ts`, `missionControlAuthentication.ts`, and two test files), caused by a local `node_modules` older than `package.json` (`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.17-preview.4 installed vs preview.5 required; `libsodium-wrappers` not installed).
- `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>` (the `precommit` script): passed.
- End-to-end on a dev build (`npm run transpile-client`, Electron 43.7.7, macOS 27.0.1), using real key presses on a system-wide `ctrl+alt+cmd+j` binding. Each result was confirmed with main-process trace logs and by polling the focused window and frontmost app:
  - Hidden with Cmd+H, editor window last focused: Agents window shown and focused, with VS Code in front, about 80 ms after the press ✅
  - VS Code active with the editor focused: Agents window focused and stayed focused ✅
  - VS Code behind another app, editor window last focused: Agents window brought to the front and focused ✅
  - New Agents window opened from the Command Palette while VS Code was active: opened focused ✅

Scenarios.Scenario: macOS system-wide Open Agents Window while the application is hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Electron global-shortcut callback selects one owning window, sends one run-action IPC to its renderer, the command makes one native-host IPC back to the main process, existing Agents-window resolution completes, then the changed path shows the single target window, activates the app, and focuses the window. The focus work is on the interaction's critical path and is the intended reveal operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatches vscode:runAction from the main process to one renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per shortcut trigger after selecting one owner, independent of the number of registered owner windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same run-action IPC routed every system-wide trigger before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The renderer must receive and run the command before the Agents window can be opened and focused.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ProxyChannel invokes the main-process native host from the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native-host IPC and await were present; only its final focus mode changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The open call must return before the target focus sequence executes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checks whether the Agents workspace file exists and writes it if absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existence check per open request; one write only on the cold first-use path where the file is missing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical filesystem work occurred before the focus-mode change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The check, and cold-path write, complete before window resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queries hidden application state, shows the target BrowserWindow, activates the macOS application, then focuses the BrowserWindow and its web contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hidden-state query, one show, one application focus, and one target focus sequence for the single returned target window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Transfer mode only attempted BrowserWindow/webContents focus, which macOS ignored while the application was hidden.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the final critical-path reveal work and corrects the hidden-app behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Shortcut trigger frequency; target-window cardinality remains one after owner selection and workspace-window reuse.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One owner is selected per shortcut event. Events are not coalesced, but workspace matching reuses a single existing Agents window; the diff adds only one constant-size focus sequence per trigger and does not add aggregate fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Window matching reuses a warm Agents window. The workspace file is written only when absent, though existence is checked per request. The changed focus path has no cache, retained keys, or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the IPC, filesystem, and native-window sequence from the traced call path; no scaling or retention mechanism was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact native show/activation duration depends on macOS and window state, but the work is constant-size, explicitly requested, and only the show is conditional on hidden state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new native operations are bounded to one target and are required to make the requested interaction progress; existing filesystem/window work and lack of trigger coalescing are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agents Window from foreground command palette, keyboard shortcut, chat action, or invitation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer makes one native-host IPC, folder intent and the Agents workspace are resolved, an existing Agents window is reused or one window is created, one selection message is sent, and the returned target is focused. On macOS the diff adds an application hidden-state query and application-focus call; while already active these are constant-size native operations. On Windows and Linux Force reaches the same BrowserWindow focus path as Transfer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Crosses from the invoking renderer to the main process and later sends vscode:selectAgentsFolder to the Agents renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request IPC and one target message for the single selected window per action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both IPC boundaries and their cardinality were unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Main-process resolution and the returned target are required before final focus; the selection message uses existing sendWhenReady behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Performs one existence check and a cold-only workspace-file write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per action and at most one cold write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same check/write path existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before reuse or creation of the Agents window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On macOS, checks app hidden state and requests application activation before the existing target-window/webContents focus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One application query and focus request for one returned window; no show call when the app is not hidden.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The target BrowserWindow and web contents were focused directly without an application-focus request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a constant native activation request immediately before final window focus.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency of explicit open actions; folder/session payload size does not multiply the changed focus work, and effective window cardinality is one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each explicit user action starts one request. There is no new limiter or sequencer, but deduplication by the Agents workspace gives an effective target cardinality of one; concurrent invocation behavior of opening/resolution predates the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm calls reuse the existing workspace window; cold calls may create/load one. No focus state is cached, and the PR does not change window matching or file caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the call is new on macOS and constant per action; low evidence for any meaningful performance outcome.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of a redundant macOS activation request while already active is platform-dependent, but there is no evidence of blocking, repeated layout, or user-visible latency beyond a constant user-triggered native call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new foreground macOS activation call is bounded and user-triggered, with no demonstrated latency, throughput, memory, or rendering regression; all heavyweight open work is pre-existing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Other Force-focus consumers reveal a target window while VS Code is hidden on macOS
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A consumer such as Focus Window, URL handling, task/debug completion, context menu handling, or notification focus reaches BaseWindow.focus(Force). The changed hidden-state branch shows the one target before the already-existing app activation and BrowserWindow/webContents focus calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer callers may invoke main-process target focus through the native-host channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC per caller request and one target window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Force-focus callers already crossed this channel and activated/focused the application.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Focus cannot complete until the main process performs the native calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Adds one hidden-state query and one BrowserWindow.show before existing application activation and target focus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per Force request and one show only while the app is hidden, for one target window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Force mode activated the app and focused the target without first showing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The show is synchronous native UI work on the reveal path, but it is required to avoid focusing the previously active window.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit Force-focus requests; no collection size or application window count multiplies the new operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each consumer request targets one window. No loop, collection fan-out, queue, or new concurrent scheduling is added by the branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hidden state is queried live because it is volatile; after the first reveal the application is no longer hidden, so subsequent requests skip show. There is no retained cache or lifecycle change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in reachability and one-call cardinality; no evidence supports a concrete negative performance symptom.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native show cost varies with target state, but the operation occurs once per hidden-app reveal and does not reconstruct hidden UI or retain resources.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The branch introduces bounded synchronous UI work only when needed to satisfy Force focus and naturally stops issuing show after the app is visible.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced the two executable hunks through global shortcut routing, native-host IPC, Agents-window resolution/reuse, filesystem initialization, BrowserWindow creation/reuse, and all Force-focus callers. The PR adds bounded native show/activation work for a single target and does not introduce scaling fan-out, repeated collection work, retained state, cache-lifecycle problems, or a concurrency burst. No valid performance findings were identified.
